Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable morphism
of algebraic spaces over $S$. Then
$f$ is affine (in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable})
if and only if for all affine schemes $Z$
and morphisms $Z \to Y$ the scheme $X \times_Y Z$ is affine.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable morphism
of algebraic spaces over $S$.
conclusions:
$f$ is affine (in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable})
if and only if for all affine schemes $Z$
and morphisms $Z \to Y$ the scheme $X \times_Y Z$ is affine.

reason: A representable morphism is affine exactly when each of its scheme base changes by an affine test has affine source, directly by the definition of affine morphism of schemes.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
For affine f, f_*O_Y is a quasi-coherent O_X-algebra with relative Spec as inverse construction.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is representable and affine,
\item $f$ is affine,
\item for every affine scheme $V$ and \'etale morphism $V \to Y$
the scheme $X \times_Y V$ is affine,
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is affine, and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is affine.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
conclusions:
for every affine scheme $V$ and \'etale morphism $V \to Y$
the scheme $X \times_Y V$ is affine,

there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is affine, and

there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such
that each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is affine.

reason: Affineness is stable under base change and may be checked after an étale scheme presentation. Descent for affine morphisms makes the local scheme test global and gives representability; Zariski locality completes all five equivalences.

The anti-equivalence has inverse given by relative Spec_X of the quasi-coherent O_X-algebra.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
There is an anti-equivalence of categories
$$
\begin{matrix}
\text{algebraic spaces} \\
\text{affine over }X
\end{matrix}
\longleftrightarrow
\begin{matrix}
\text{quasi-coherent sheaves} \\
\text{of }\mathcal{O}_X\text{-algebras}
\end{matrix}
$$
which associates to $f : Y \to X$ the sheaf $f_*\mathcal{O}_Y$.
Moreover, this equivalence is compatible with arbitrary base change.
hypotheses: Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.

reason: The source constructs relative Spec using an étale affine groupoid and checks the affine presentation and descended algebra, but explicitly omits verification of the equivalence relation on W⇒V (line 3813) and compatibility with arbitrary base change (line 3830), both substantive parts of the reviewed anti-equivalence.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$.
Let $A$ be an Artinian ring. Any morphism $\Spec(A) \to X$ is affine.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$.
Let $A$ be an Artinian ring.

reason: For an étale affine chart U→X, the pullback Spec A×_XU is a quasi-compact étale scheme over an Artinian base. Its underlying points form a finite discrete set and the scheme criterion makes it affine. Affineness can be checked étale-locally on X, so Spec A→X is affine.
